intro:
KAMISATO ESTATE — PROJECT RECAP & END CREDITS
Recorded 26 September 2026

A place to arrive, work, read, play, and sit quietly with Ayaka.

This is a retrospective of the major work recorded in the repository, its
implementation ledger and release evidence. It groups the project into chapters;
it is not a claim that every historical experiment remains in the final build.
size:
The pre-credits delivery (source fedae857) measured 81,195,193 bytes:
81.20 MB in decimal units, or 77.43 MiB in binary units. Some transfer tools
display the latter number even when their label loosely says “MB”. That can
explain a “70-something” display for that delivery. It cannot, by itself, explain a fall
from 120 MB to 70 MB.

The substantial reductions happened during development and packaging:

• One painting, fewer copies. Early packaging could include several responsive
  sizes of the same painting. A 6 September commit records about 30 MB of
  redundant image sizes being excluded, leaving a 121.7 MB drop-in at that point.
  The original-size painting remained available inside the single file.

• One format instead of two. A 14 September commit records approximately
  160 MB becoming 98 MB when the single-file builder stopped embedding JPEG
  paintings alongside their WebP twins. This is a historical build measurement,
  not proof that the particular copy Kellen remembers was that exact build.

• More efficient text and asset packing. The cycle 14 audit measured
  98,195,993 → 92,275,965 bytes, saving 5.92 MB. Text assets were stored as text
  instead of base64, identical assets were shared, and files useful only to a
  web host were excluded. The builder also avoids a second copy of embedded
  fonts: its source documents roughly 12 MB of otherwise duplicated base64.

• Better image encoding. Cycle 85 converted eight tea-room heroes and fourteen
  assistant portraits to WebP. The recorded raw-image saving was 9,445,471 bytes,
  corresponding to roughly 12.6 MB in the base64-heavy HTML package. That step
  included lossy image encoding: the story is not exclusively lossless packing.

• Continued optimisation and replacement art. Repeated translation tables,
  unused code and redundant data were reduced; later artwork and features also
  added bytes back. The pre-credits delivery changed from 82,833,210 bytes
  to 81,195,193 bytes: a further reduction of about 1.64 MB. These are sequential
  snapshots, not a list of independent savings to add together.

The full design collection is separate from the playable file. The 32 upscaled
8K wallpaper PNG masters alone total about 1.04 GB; their full-size WebPs total
166.8 MB. Runtime derivatives are used in the app. The optional local AI pack is
also separate: 453,374,202 bytes, approximately 453 MB. It is not embedded in
the HTM or in the public website build.

A normal file copy does not silently discard artwork or features. If a received
file has exactly the same bytes, it has exactly the same content, regardless of
the displayed units. If the received uncompressed file really is around
70,000,000 bytes, that is not this exact 81,195,193-byte release; it could be a
different build or package. Without that copy, the transfer-specific reason
cannot be established. File size alone also does not establish image resolution.
scale:
The numbered development record reaches Cycle 173, with many audit and
implementation batches inside individual cycles. Further integration, artwork,
credits and finishing passes continued without new cycle numbers. Cycle numbers
are separate from commits, tests and calendar days.

The Git history begins on 3 September 2026. This release was delivered on
26 September: 23 elapsed calendar days, covering 24 calendar dates. That is the
recorded development span, not a measurement of continuous working hours or any
planning before the first commit.

At release-record commit e0dbce02, the current branch contains 1,381 commits.
The tracked source under src/ contains 209,652 lines. Source, server, scripts and
tests together contain 369,402 lines of the counted code-file types. These counts
include comments, blank lines and embedded data; they are not all executable logic
or a measure of manually typed code. That pre-credits local suite passed 6,682 tests. The later credits release
(source 9386c72) passed 6,702 local tests and its GitHub checks.
story:
1. From a welcome page to an interactive estate

The project grew from an IIS landing-page foundation into a themed application
with a front gate, main hall, White Heron Room, tea room, courtyard and map.
Navigation acquired remembered preferences, menus, shortcuts, room links and
an uncluttered Estate View. The main dashboard was organised into Overview,
Network, Markets, Study, Lab and Desk wings.

The dashboard was also made more honest. Invented prices, random-walk charts
and decorative server numbers were replaced with real requests, local browser
measurements, dated captured responses or explicit unavailable states. Clocks,
weather, currency conversion and the request inspector became working tools.

2. A consistent atmosphere

The estate gained time-of-day paintings, phone and desktop compositions, a
Japanese clock, weather effects, petals, lighting, sound controls, quiet modes,
reduced-motion support and BANKAI effects. English, Chinese and Japanese reached
the rooms, games, tools, handbook and helpers through many rounds of correction.

The visual direction evolved toward restrained gold, readable glass, visible
wallpaper colours and less clutter. Kellen repeatedly steered the result toward
elegance and a quieter atmosphere, including softer gold, better figure framing,
more plausible lighting and a more natural pond.

3. Doors, travel and a map that agrees with its paintings

The entrance and travel animation evolved into shoji-style doors. The latest
correction keeps the old scene covered while the destination loads and uses
readiness checks before opening. Separate map flight, flash and ink transitions
were removed from that travel path. Retry and Back recovery were tested.

The map grew to five destinations, with pan, zoom, visited states and four
paintings. Each time-of-day painting now has its own target coordinates because
the buildings are framed differently. Pin labels were separated from their
anchors, and phone info-card placement was corrected. The final map evidence
records 18 passing cases and 260 checks, including recovery tests.

Estate View was corrected to keep the current place and wallpaper while hiding
the interface. Space can trigger BANKAI there; Escape or the menu restores the
controls. Typing, open dialogs and game controls retain their own key handling.

4. Ayaka's tea room

The tea room acquired landscape and portrait paintings, time-of-day variants,
local prerecorded speech in three languages, steam and atmosphere, a command
bar and translation tools. The voice clips are selected synthetic voices, not
the game's official performance or a clone of its actor.

Chess, Go, Matcha Match and Konpira Fune Fune became playable tables with their
own controls, rules and records. A digital tea ritual added warm/add/pour/rest/
serve interactions, a real rest timer and a record of completed sittings.
The translation fallback identifies exact phrasebook matches instead of
inventing translations. The private tea-room build uses an encrypted seal;
the open visitor editions use the publication pipeline's open-room variant.

5. A courtyard full of games

The courtyard became a pavilion for Sakura 2048, Koi, Lantern Sweeper, picture
puzzles, Petal Catch, Falling Blocks, Sudoku, the terrarium and the record book.
Together with the tea-room tables, these were developed as actual games with
rules, progress, controls, endings and save behaviour, rather than static demos.

Work included difficulties, daily challenges where supported, hints, scoring,
undo or takeback where appropriate, pause/resume, touch gestures, keyboard
controls, focus modes, sound/mute controls and records that distinguish modes.
The terrarium acquired growth, watering, species, calendar/light behaviour,
away reports and completion conditions. Scores and local progress join backups.

6. Koi became a substantial game of its own

Koi grew through classic and modern play, Zen and Super Zen, Royale, a fish
library, fish families, powers, rank progression, lives, petal rules, rival AI,
endings, podiums and record categories. The current main roster has 205 fish
across ten families, plus a separate developer fish. Multiplayer room plumbing
and host/guest play were implemented too; that history is not a claim that every
network combination was re-tested in this last release.

The fish renderer went through repeated work on body paths, tails, eyes, scales,
materials, markings, swimming motion, camera placement and rendering cost.
The interface gained foldaway settings and a quiet view so the pond can occupy
the screen. Phone fit, overlays and control placement received further fixes.

The latest four pond paintings share the mossy-stone, open-water reference:
soft morning, jade afternoon, restrained evening light and readable teal night.
The runtime tint was lightened so the paintings remain visible. Versioned image
URLs prevent an old cached pond painting from masquerading as the new one.

The last visual audit caught a real defect after ordinary checks passed: a
Royale fish crossing the pond boundary could stretch into a line across the
whole screen. The fix keeps neighbouring body segments together in drawing
coordinates. Deterministic edge tests, live desktop/phone gameplay and the
actual Safari standalone file were checked afterwards.

7. A library and a working study

The estate gained a three-language Bible reader, page turns, search, bookmarks,
highlights and remembered places. Quotes, a phrase browser, favourites and
classical reading material expanded the library.

The practical cards include a focus timer, study checklist, spaced-repetition
flashcards, formula reference, Big-O reference, prompt library, notebook,
deadlines, reading list and GPA/CAP calculator. The Lab adds token/cost and VRAM
estimates, classifier metrics, tensor-shape tools, activation plots, learning-rate
schedules, matrix operations, Bayes calculations and unit conversion.

8. A browser-local workspace

The Desk wing gained a Notion-inspired workspace: nested pages, 31 block types,
rich text, slash commands, drag/reorder, search, favourites, trash, comments,
backlinks, icons, covers and templates. Database views include table, board,
list, gallery, calendar, timeline, chart and form, with filters, sorts, grouping,
relations, rollups and formulas.

Calendar work added day/week time lanes, quarter-hour dragging, recurrence,
reminders and import/export. Undo, persisted page history, media handling,
cover positioning, cancellation and backup/restore received dedicated fixes.
Keyboard ownership, selection, search and narrow-screen behaviour were audited.
It remains a local workspace, not the complete Notion cloud service: there is
no automatic cloud account, collaboration or cross-device sync.

9. Smarter assistants, with explicit limits

Thoma and Wu Ze Tian began with handwritten rules and estate knowledge. They
gained navigation, settings control, arithmetic, conversions, game help,
follow-ups, taught facts and labelled external lookups where available.

Later work connected the estate assistant and workspace AI actions to an
optional local model. It added bounded context, retrieval from local stores,
explicit memory and a validated action layer with receipts and Undo for
supported operations. The workspace gained model-backed writing and page
questions when the model is available. Evaluation also addressed invented
steps, missing note clauses, language drift, timeouts and cancellation.

The core estate works without the model. The plain HTM does not contain its
453 MB weights; model availability depends on the supported environment and
pack. Rule-based help remains the fallback. The assistants have a defined action
set; they are not unrestricted agents that can do literally everything.

10. The visual overhaul and the 8K collection

The art work included reference-based drafts, comparisons and selections for
the gate, overview/map, courtyard, White Heron Room and tea room. Lighting,
colour, portrait framing and Ayaka's proportions were refined. The wider art
work also covered assistant expressions, tea-ritual illustrations, map art,
workspace covers, empty states and game scenery.

Thirty-two approved wallpaper compositions were exported as 8K masters:
20 landscapes at 7680×4320 and 12 portraits at 4320×7680. These are upscaled
exports from smaller generated inputs, not native 8K detail. The application
uses runtime derivatives; it does not embed every full-resolution master.
The four newest Koi paintings also have verified 7680×4320 upscaled 8K
masters, enlarged from their native 1672×941 originals. This brings the
archived set at that stage to 36 upscaled 8K compositions. The game keeps efficient
1672×941 WebP versions for smooth loading; the separate 8K masters are
not embedded in the complete HTM. Upscaling does not make them native 8K.

11. The engineering underneath the calm surface

Many cycles addressed loading, lazy modules, image decoding, canvas resolution,
GPU cost, background loops, hidden tabs and adaptive effects. Battery Saver,
Baseline and Ultra modes were added. Local inference yields to active gameplay.
Build-size limits and regression checks made the cost of new features visible.

Other work covered accessibility, focus traps, Escape behaviour, reduced motion,
storage failure, interrupted gestures, cross-tab writes, encrypted-room recovery,
network failures, service-worker updates, stale caches, deep links and backup
validation. Server routes and request handling received security and abuse tests.

These measures improve behaviour; they do not certify zero lag on every device,
universal 8K/120 fps or the absence of every possible future bug.

12. Packaging, review and delivery

The project ships as a web build and a self-contained HTM, with an optional
separate AI pack. Fonts, voices, artwork and reference data can be bundled
locally. Live services retain their network requirements and dated fallbacks.
The web edition has service-worker/offline-readiness work; the standalone file
does not need to download its embedded assets to display them.

The release process now builds the HTM directly from known build outputs,
writes it atomically, and records the source stamp, exact size and SHA-256.
It avoids depending on an old development server's cached download response.
Both GitHub Pages editions were published and checked against the built files.

The pre-credits application source was fedae857, with release records at
e0dbce02. Its build, 6,682 local tests and source GitHub check passed. Native Safari covered six routes through the actual delivered
file. The final Royale checks covered two viewports, sixteen checks and fourteen
reviewed frames. Other map, art and BANKAI evidence retains its actual build
identity rather than being relabelled as if every historical test ran again.

13. A keepsake and cinematic credits

The shared project story can be opened from About the estate, a two-second
crest hold, a library keepsake, the handbook, the command palette and the estate
assistants. Its perspective crawl and readable chapters share the same archive, fully
available in English, Chinese and Japanese through the language setting.
Pause, Restart and Close remain available; reduced motion keeps the text still.
Two-finger trackpad scrolling and arrow keys glide through the cinematic
credits in either direction, pausing autoplay. Play resumes from that point.
The credits share the estate’s glass fill, frost, border and shadow tokens.
Bright serif lettering and a compact text shadow preserve readability while
keeping the wallpaper visible through the same material as the other panels.

14. A wind-chime garden

The small garden pavilion beside the bamboo, left of the pond, became a quiet
sightseeing stop on the map. Its two views pair autumn maples with a clear
glass bell, and a cool green summer forest with a blue Rimuru slime chime.
Both have morning, afternoon, evening and night paintings. Estate time
guides the light, with a manual override; daylight shifts gently as time passes.

Occasional gusts move the foliage and the hanging parts together. Leaf rustle
follows the breeze. Each chime sounds when its clapper visibly reaches the
glass, with subtle differences in strength and ringing colour. Sound begins
softly on entry, with a mute control, and rests when the view is hidden.
Visitors can switch designs or enable a ten-minute rotation; the shared doors
cover each design change until the next view is ready. Hidden controls and
full screen make the garden a quiet display to leave on a monitor.

The eight wind-chime backgrounds have verified 7680×4320 upscaled 8K archive masters, bringing the wallpaper archive to 44 compositions. The garden displays 3840×2160 WebP derivatives and separate transparent bell artwork. These are enlarged from generated originals, not native 8K detail.
credits:
Creator, commissioner and creative director — Kellen Quek Zai He · 郭再赫
The estate's purpose, character, selections and final visual standards; the
feedback that kept returning the work to elegance, clarity and a quieter pond.

Principal implementation and development partner — Claude
Much of the feature construction, game logic, interface work, audit cycles,
refactoring and handover documentation recorded throughout the project.

Art iteration, independent review, integration and final delivery — Astra / Codex
Wallpaper and interface exploration, reference-based image work, browser
inspection, bug hunting, performance investigation, cross-agent coordination,
regression fixes, artifact verification and release completion.

Supporting review and implementation — delegated assistant agents
Focused work across rooms, artwork, map geometry, game rendering, testing and
independent reviews. Their findings and the coordinator's checks combined;
an individual agent's pass was not treated as proof of the entire estate.

Image creation and finishing — AI image generation, followed by selection,
local export/encoding and the separately documented Real-ESRGAN 8K upscale work.

Engineering foundation — React, TypeScript, Vite, browser Canvas/WebGL,
browser storage, WebLLM/MLC for optional local inference, and the supporting
open-source libraries, fonts and tools recorded in the repository.

Character and world inspiration — Kamisato Ayaka and Genshin Impact.
This is an independently built fan project, not an official game release.

The signature brief — softer gold; clear, readable glass; doors that hide the
wait; a map that takes you where it points; and fish that deserve their pond.

FROM A LANDING PAGE TO A PLACE OF YOUR OWN.

— Kellen Quek Zai He · 郭再赫
